title: checker: mcx with a wire[2] bundle in its control list fires on one wire (ISA 0.9 §4.4)
description: What: in 'action @a (p:wire mut, q:wire mut) (c:wire[2] in) () () (); swap p q; mcx (c) p', bennett-check (e5bc3af) flips p at c=1 (c[0]=1, c[1]=0). §4.4: mcx is 'X on the target iff all controls are |1>'. Reading (c) as both wires of c, p must stay 0 (checker-replay: proof over 16 elements); if a bundle is not a legal control-list entry the object is ill-formed and must be rejected as such. The binary's result matches neither. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/mcx-bundle-control (E_CERT_REPLAY tuple mismatch at element 1). title: checker: ashr by shift >= N sign-fills instead of 0 (ISA 0.9 §4.1, §11.1)

Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/ashr-shift-ge-n (E_CERT_REPLAY tuple mismatch at element 132, replayed t=15 expected t=0; checker-replay agrees with the table, evidence 1/256). Found by checker-replay differential (6af3243).

title: checker: lift.const negative literal spelling replays as 0 (ISA 0.9 §3.3)
description: What: bennett-check (built from e5bc3af) replays 'c = lift.const.i4 -1; r = lift.xor x0 c' with c = 0; §3.3 says a literal c with -2^(N-1) <= c < 2^N denotes c mod 2^N and both spellings are accepted, so c = 15 and t(x0=0) = 15. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/const-negative-spelling (bennett-check reports E_CERT_REPLAY 'tuple mismatch at element 0 ... replayed {bundles:[0,0,0]} but expected {bundles:[0,15,0]}'; checker-replay replays the table as evidence 1/256). Found by checker-replay differential (6af3243). Either fix the literal decode or, if -1 is rejected, reject the object with a §3.3 diagnostic, never a silent 0.

title: Rung 1: LLVM18-compatible Rust and Julia frontends required
description:
The requested dual-major scalar rung includes Rust and Julia on LLVM18, never an omitted language. Installed rustc 1.99.1 emits LLVM23.1.1; Julia 1.13.3 code_llvm emits LLVM20.1.8. All source native O0/O2 oracles compile/run, but LLVM18 cannot read their current stock IR. Dialect @023f5a7 §19.8: "An input newer than M is BD-E-VERSION." This is a toolchain prerequisite, not an illegal scalar or a plugin refusal. Install and publish compatible stock Rust/Julia frontends that emit LLVM<=18 and fit the legality envelope, with explicit paths/version recording; otherwise coordinate the frontend/major matrix with the dialect owner. Do not rewrite/downgrade IR, drop languages or count this as a skip. Reproduce commands:
/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/llvm-link /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-1/20261101T132057.475661Z/Rust/18/input.bc /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung1-bennett-runtimes-6808622d560b2e301c635c205eecde3d932b6df5/dist/llvm18/bennett-runtimes.bc /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung1-bennett-arith-249e6192b95c6dbbb875510c32a677ba113e9af5/dist/llvm18/bennett-arith.bc --only-needed -o /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-1/20261101T132057.475661Z/Rust/18/r1_sat_add/linked.bc
/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/llvm-link /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-1/20261101T132057.475661Z/Julia/18/ir/r1_sat_add.ll /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung1-bennett-runtimes-6808622d560b2e301c635c205eecde3d932b6df5/dist/llvm18/bennett-runtimes.bc /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung1-bennett-arith-249e6192b95c6dbbb875510c32a677ba113e9af5/dist/llvm18/bennett-arith.bc --only-needed -o /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-1/20261101T132057.475661Z/Julia/18/r1_sat_add/linked.bc
Observed: Invalid attribute group entry (Producer LLVM23.1.1 / Reader LLVM18.1.3); Julia getelementptr inbounds nuw: expected type. Evidence /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-1/20261101T132057.475661Z
close_reason: Orchestrator ruling 2026-11-01: not a blocker. North Star §8 rung 1 requires both executors equal to native, not both LLVM majors per language. Dialect §19.8 forbids inputs newer than M but accepts older ones, so the matrix is: C on LLVM 18 and 23 (stock clang of each major); Rust on LLVM 23 (stock rustc 1.99.1 emits 23.1.1 IR; 18 only if a stock rustc with LLVM<=18 is installed, not required); Julia on LLVM 23 (stock Julia 1.13.3 emits LLVM 20.1.8 IR, which the 23 pipeline reads). The rung-1 gate's matrix should be adjusted to this (mark Rust/18 and Julia/18 as 'not applicable: stock frontend emits IR newer than M (§19.8)', not FAIL); the remaining Rust/Julia blockers are the plugin beads bp-xb8 (Rust personality) and bp-zeg (Julia gcstack entry state), and bp-75y for the exhaustive full-D rows.

title: Rung-4 estimate: use ideal-all-to-all target and full N=2^20 launch; adapter accepts bound pins (from bennett-estimate)
description:
Source: bennett-estimate/.tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md, "Consumer follow-up for bennett-conformance: rung-4 estimate inputs and capacity" (queued consumer fix; not a restriction of the full rung and not a request to adopt an unpublished ISA policy).

Determination: the rung-4 estimate consumer in bennett-conformance has no full-launch input and uses an infeasible target. Evidence: (1) the only available .tmp/rung-4/runs objects are reduced rung4-mini.bennett diagnostics (20261101T213213.441081Z and 20261101T221646.155856Z) with ISA/object/launch/sched/cert 0.8 headers, four lprocs and a 16-byte data image, not the actual N=2^20 launch; the estimator pins the published complete ref 0.9 library and no ref 0.8 expansion is published, so applying 0.9 costs to the legacy diagnostic would invent a binding; a full modern launch artifact remains required. (2) The named target in rung-4 DESIGN §6, superconducting-grid-illustrative.json, has data.capacity=16 and buffer.capacity=4; ISA §8.4/§11 require class capacity, and the required 2^28-wire interface fits neither class (nor their sum), so reporting a feasible exact cost under it would be false.

Proposed exact change to ladder/rung-4/DESIGN.md §6 and its pinned target entry: "Use the published ideal-all-to-all.json named target for the full N=2^20 resource forecast. Its logical data class is unbounded. Bind its exact target hash and report reference-construction costs under the unchanged complete launch object, resolved arguments and budget tuple. Retain the finite superconducting-grid-illustrative.json model as an explicit infeasibility diagnostic. Do not reduce the database, register width, program, oracle count or quantum domain to fit that small target."
Also: pass the resolved subject/arguments/budget to the estimator adapter and accept its bound object_hash, target_hash, invocation.budget, resources and exact_resources fields (or add explicit aliases) instead of relying on a zero-budget CLI default to infer pins.json. The specs fix bindings, not the adapter spelling.

description: What: on controlled-action-09 as published in bennett-isa-spec (run without --target/--schedule), 15 table mutants (drop/dup/swap/flip/short/long/noncanonical/number/out_of_range/row_field/tuple_field) are rejected by checker-replay (E_REPLAY_MISMATCH/E_REPLAY_TABLE) and left unchecked by bennett-check ('target document is missing'). The replay's reject relies on a legal realisation of the scheduled subject agreeing with its reference semantics on basis states; the comparison relation (§12.1) is realised-vs-table. Schema faults (row_field, tuple_field, number, noncanonical, short, long) are definitive regardless; the value mismatches assume that agreement. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/table-without-target. Decide whether the replay should report value mismatches without a target as unchecked.

title: checker: capability boundary seen by the differential (lproc, memory rows, H/Z/H and T/Tdg actions, adj call) and a 120 s timeout on arith.bij.addmod.w8.mfb
description: What: checker-replay replays these synthetic claims (hand-derived facts, checker-replay/checker_replay/synthetic.py) while bennett-check (e5bc3af) reports unchecked: lproc-depth-limit, lproc-recursive-sum, lproc-stack-monotonic, lproc-step-budget, oracle-alloc-zero-bumps, oracle-double-free, oracle-free-pinned, oracle-global-load, oracle-heap-limit, oracle-load-past-end, oracle-parmov, oracle-store-load-heap (evidence) and action-adj-call, action-hzh, action-ttdg (proof). Consistent with docs/checker.md's stated boundary; listed so the extension has ready witnesses. Separately the debug binary exceeded the harness's 120 s per-case timeout on the published bennett-arith/adders/objects/arith.bij.addmod.w8.mfb.bisa (and two of its object mutants) on a loaded host (load ~30); checker-replay finishes it (proof on both exhaustive claims, overall unchecked for out-of-scope items). Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/lproc-recursive-sum, oracle-store-load-heap, action-hzh, timeout-addmod-w8.

title: checker: reports unchecked where a claim is definitively ill-formed (absent subject/program closure, oracle relation on an action)
description: What: for an object with no imports section, bennett-check (e5bc3af) reports unchecked ('subject region is not in the supplied object', 'expected program is not in the supplied object') where no linked library can supply the closure, and unchecked for expected "oracle" on an action subject (§12.1: the oracle relation compares to §5.2's oracle map and needs an oracle). checker-replay rejects all three (E_REPLAY_SUBJECT/E_REPLAY_EXPECTED). Not unsound (nothing accepted), but weaker than the spec allows. Counts in diff2: 49 + 49 + 3 mutants. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/unchecked-subject-closure-absent, unchecked-program-absent, unchecked-oracle-on-action.
